base_blocks.text: I'd stop there and not test it, even when it sounds like a prediction.

path: When the Adult Voice Feels Fake
Two Common Guarding Patterns Blocking Reparenting
base_blocks.text: Two Common Guarding Patterns Blocking Reparenting

path: When the Adult Voice Feels Fake
Two Common Guarding Patterns Blocking Reparenting
base_blocks.text: One of these patterns is a skeptic, on duty all the time: "You're just making this up." It may have spent years keeping you from being humiliated or abandoned again, and it has probably watched you get excited about other healing things before that got unexplainedly dropped a month later. We do need some skepticism, so thank it for keeping you on track.

path: When the Adult Voice Feels Fake
Two Common Guarding Patterns Blocking Reparenting
base_blocks.text: The other one shows up when you get close to some painful memory or insight. Suddenly you'd rather check your phone, or do anything aside from directly feeling it (even a yawn can come with an "I'm so done with this" feeling). Maybe this guard doesn't believe there's a grown-up around who could handle what's coming? That yawn might actually be the opposite of checking out, though. Re-evaluation Counseling, a global movement of peer counseling, counts yawning as productive emotional discharge, a feeling on its way out. The skeptic and the pull both started out guarding you against something that really hurt. If you treat either one like an enemy, it'll probably just think "See? I knew it," and it stays on the payroll since guards require attackers.

path: When the Adult Voice Feels Fake
Two Common Guarding Patterns Blocking Reparenting
base_blocks.text: The Belief Behind the Guards

path: When the Adult Voice Feels Fake
Two Common Guarding Patterns Blocking Reparenting
base_blocks.text: Say you learned somewhere along the way that if you need someone, they end up leaving you. You probably never said it to yourself in words, but it steers you before you know why. That pull of distraction is one way of dealing with it. Many folks will also find themselves going along with things they don't really prefer, or else insisting they don't need anybody (sour grapes). Some people pleasers go along for months as if nothing's wrong while the pressure builds and then they blow up out of nowhere. Then they feel so bad about it they go right back to going along to get along. With any of these patterns, I'd ask what it's protecting you from, because it doesn't really help to just label it a bad habit. (Sometimes a sweet is just a sweet, though, not an escape, as The Inner Guide gets into.)

path: When the Adult Voice Feels Fake
Two Common Guarding Patterns Blocking Reparenting
base_blocks.text: You're actually a prophet, but you didn't know it! Have you ever heard of a self-fulfilling prophecy? Say nobody ever hears that you're struggling, since you didn't think they'd want to. Then nobody offers to help, and that can look like proof nobody cares. Keeping quiet might have been the smartest thing you could do back then, with nobody safe to tell, but now, if there are people who are safely available, it can keep help away.

path: When the Adult Voice Feels Fake
base_blocks.text: Hear the Guard First

path: When the Adult Voice Feels Fake
base_blocks.text: Whichever protective part showed up, try talking to it in the same Nurturer voice you meant for your little one. At some point you can ask that part, "What are you afraid would happen if you stepped back?"

path: When the Adult Voice Feels Fake
base_blocks.text: It might say this will just be one more performance, and you'll fool yourself again. That one can sting, because there could be something to it. Maybe you've fooled yourself before, and that part remembers. "Tell me what you remember, I'm listening." works well here. It puts you into the role of the Nurturer, which alleviates the instinct to argue back. Usually your little one only comes forward after that part feels heard. Peek-a-boo! If you push past it, you might get exactly the performance it was afraid of. Even if you didn't win an Emmy last year, that can look convincing, with the right words and maybe even tears, while nothing underneath feels any safer.

path: When the Adult Voice Feels Fake
base_blocks.text: A harder voice can seem more fitting for something that's been in your way. I'd still keep the Nurturer voice. If that voice isn't there in you yet, borrow it from someone who's been safe for you.

path: When the Adult Voice Feels Fake
Earning its trust, day to day
base_blocks.text: Earning its trust, day to day

path: When the Adult Voice Feels Fake
Earning its trust, day to day
base_blocks.text: A new roommate doesn't win you over with a speech on move-in day (hopefully, right?). The rent just has to keep showing up. Your Protector earns that guard's trust about the same way, mostly out in ordinary life. The things you do can be small, like keeping a promise to yourself nobody else knew about. Or saying no to someone, and not texting an hour later to take it back. That second one can be really hard.

path: When the Adult Voice Feels Fake
base_blocks.text: If it won't step back

path: When the Adult Voice Feels Fake
base_blocks.text: That part doesn't have to move out. It's been living there way longer than the grown-up you. It can keep watch while you take one small step toward your little one. I think watching is what it wants anyway, to find out if there's a grown-up here now who could call it all off if things got to be too much. It doesn't have to be all or nothing, either. Maybe it would settle for a lighter cover for now, like blinds tilted open a crack, and let you peek out for a minute (ST-CA, section 9.3.4). If it says no, I'd listen. When it lets you, keep an eye on that part too, for any change at all.

path: When the Adult Voice Feels Fake
If it's been calling all this stupid
base_blocks.text: If it's been calling all this stupid

path: When the Adult Voice Feels Fake
If it's been calling all this stupid
base_blocks.text: It might turn out to be scared of getting its hopes up. I wouldn't want to get mine up either. I'd tell it something like, "You don't have to hope yet, I'll keep coming back even when I mess up." Sometimes it doesn't say anything back for a while.

path: When the Adult Voice Feels Fake
If it all feels like your fault
base_blocks.text: If it all feels like your fault

path: When the Adult Voice Feels Fake
If it all feels like your fault
base_blocks.text: Blaming yourself can be doing a protective job, too. "It's all my fault" might be your parent's line, word for word. Then again, if it's your fault, maybe you can fix it before they leave. I'd stop the cruelty either way. And I'd get curious about what makes it so hard to give up.

path: When the Adult Voice Feels Fake
base_blocks.text: When to Change the Strategy

path: When the Adult Voice Feels Fake
base_blocks.text: Weeks in and nothing much is changing? I’d want to quit too, or else keep doing the exact same thing forever so I never have to find out what's underneath this. Before going with either of those paths, look for what exactly is in the way. Sometimes the strategy was not actually implemented, just read about or played around with lightly. Or there wasn't the right environment to really practice it, like no alone time. Or perhaps you did sit down with your little one, but it felt scary or like some part of you was trying to protect you from going deeper. Whatever it turns out to be, it makes sense to work on that blocker instead of giving up on everything.

path: When the Adult Voice Feels Fake
When your kind words sound empty
base_blocks.text: When your kind words sound empty

path: When the Adult Voice Feels Fake
When your kind words sound empty
base_blocks.text: Maybe the words are all there, but the loving grown-up behind them isn’t, not yet. Some people at that point might try saying sweeter and sweeter things, and then upon that not working, perhaps just “throw the baby out with the bathwater,” and decide reparenting is a scam. I’d borrow that grown-up first. Then try again, and see if your little one can tell the difference.

path: When the Adult Voice Feels Fake
base_blocks.text: If the relief doesn't last

path: When the Adult Voice Feels Fake
base_blocks.text: Let's say an exercise leaves you feeling lighter for a few hours, but then the old feeling comes back later on. Some relief is nice, but we still want to know if we are fixing the problem at a deeper level and integrating the benefits into regular life (like texting a friend that you're having a rough day rather than saying you're fine). Jot down what changed and how long it lasted. Although if that feeds into your OCD patterns, drop it.

path: When the Adult Voice Feels Fake
How many tries would I give it?
base_blocks.text: How many tries would I give it?

path: When the Adult Voice Feels Fake
How many tries would I give it?
base_blocks.text: It's not like we can just put a number on it. Some things shift in a day. Others take about as long as learning guitar. But do notice if progress is stagnating. If it’s making things worse, or you just can’t do it right now, I’d change course sooner (stopping counts).

path: When the Adult Voice Feels Fake
base_blocks.text: If you'd rather stop

path: When the Adult Voice Feels Fake
base_blocks.text: Not wanting to do it anymore might be reason enough, but if that “nope” sounds like a part of you that’s trying to protect you, I’d hear it out first to get a better understanding.

path: When the Adult Voice Feels Fake
If you keep following the reparenting steps correctly without getting the expected results
base_blocks.text: If you keep following the reparenting steps correctly without getting the expected results

path: When the Adult Voice Feels Fake
If you keep following the reparenting steps correctly without getting the expected results
base_blocks.text: Consider if you have a unique case these steps don’t match yet. Maybe you’ll find something that works better for you, or you can ask me what I’d do for this case, or ask a therapist you work with. Either way, I’d like to hear about it!

path: When the Adult Voice Feels Fake
When the Urge to Escape Arrives
base_blocks.text: When the Urge to Escape Arrives

path: When the Adult Voice Feels Fake
When the Urge to Escape Arrives
base_blocks.text: Sometimes the urge to get away from what’s coming up emotionally gets a lot bigger. All of a sudden you need a drink, or that ex doesn’t seem so bad after all. Some people start a whole new business. If that’s you, it might mean you got close to something that really hurts, and that can be progress, honestly! I’d thank whatever part of you came up with the escape plan, and slow down. If it’s more than you can hold right now, I’d get someone steady with you.

path: When the Adult Voice Feels Fake
When the Urge to Escape Arrives
base_blocks.text: Intensive Meditation and Psychedelics

path: When the Adult Voice Feels Fake
When the Urge to Escape Arrives
base_blocks.text: So why not just blast right past that part, with intensive meditation or psychedelics? Both can get you past the guards before there’s a grown-up big enough to hold whatever comes through, so I’d hold off until there’s enough Nurturer and Protector around. How much is enough depends partly on the medicine and what therapy is done with it.

path: When the Adult Voice Feels Fake
When the Urge to Escape Arrives
base_blocks.text: Like MDMA, San Pedro is more protective and nurturing than many other medicines, especially at lower doses, so you don’t need as much Nurturer and Protector built up for those, though you still need some. Some people benefit more from solo therapy, while others benefit more from having a trained therapist guide the experience.

path: Altered States Can Deepen the Therapy
base_blocks.text: Altered States Can Deepen the Therapy

path: Altered States Can Deepen the Therapy
base_blocks.text: I’d learn to do inner-child therapy sober first, in your ordinary mindstate, since that’s the one you’ll be living in. Cars don’t start at 60mph, that’s not the way the universe seems to work. First gear leads to second leads to third, etc. Second gear, in this case, may refer to gentle meditation or self-hypnosis. When you’re ready, my self-hypnosis guide and lucid-dreaming guide can take those deeper, into third gear. Low doses of entheogens can also synergize compatibly with various gears: cactus, CBD tea with sublingual mapacho, Loveyhuasca, iboga, and so on.

path: Altered States Can Deepen the Therapy
base_blocks.text: Remember those guards from The Urge to Escape, above? Same deal here, so get enough Nurturer and Protector in the room before you go deep. Borrowed is fine, as long as it’s from someone steady who won’t try to run your trip for you. But feeling attacked by a demon on a psychedelic is not necessarily paranoia. It can be real, and it’s also not bad unless you’re unprepared. It can be supremely empowering when you can send love and see how it fixes the situation.

path: Altered States Can Deepen the Therapy
What to Do With a Peak
base_blocks.text: What to Do With a Peak

path: Altered States Can Deepen the Therapy
What to Do With a Peak
base_blocks.text: Now, the beautiful stuff. Say one night (on a psychedelic, in a dream, ten days into a meditation retreat, whatever) you felt more love than you knew was possible. Wonderful, and it matters! Keep it as a reference point, and chase it playfully, because it is already a part of you, and you’ll be like a cat chasing its tail, which can be cute and fun, or dizzy and absurd!

path: Altered States Can Deepen the Therapy
What to Do With a Peak
base_blocks.text: Jack Kornfield has a whole book on what comes next, After the Ecstasy, the Laundry. The title kind of says it all. That night can't be the bar for every morning after, or regular life starts to feel like failing. And gorgeous as it was, it doesn't mean you're done healing. The laundry will tell you more, and it's the same test as in Timing Is Individual, further down.

path: Altered States Can Deepen the Therapy
What to Do With a Peak
base_blocks.text: One reason the peak is so momentary is because we often don’t need to truly give anything up to get it. Say you’re still pretty angry, and you want enlightenment, but it has to come with the money and the partner in one package. Ketamine can get you to a peak anyway. Then, you might now have some kind of transcendental “understanding” glimpse that seems like it could fix everything, if only you could be more aware of it, which often leads into a cycle of taking more and more medicine over time. I’d prefer to ask if any of the discontent has been let go, or the anger? If not, that peak was less the love we’re after here than “I’ll be grateful once I’ve got it all,” the gratitude with conditions from Ask God for a Loan.

path: Altered States Can Deepen the Therapy
What to Do With a Peak
base_blocks.text: And if your little one still can’t take the love in? Hold off on going for bigger, crazier breakthroughs, however tempting it is, or at least know that they are a double-edged sword. Something’s in the way, and getting to know it is your next job. Often it’s a protective part that’s seen love come with strings before. Hear it out first, the way you did in Hear the Guard First.

path: Altered States Can Deepen the Therapy
base_blocks.text: When Escape Leaves Reality Behind

path: Altered States Can Deepen the Therapy
base_blocks.text: All kinds of psychoactive drugs can mess with your sense of what’s real, and that’s often the point of them, so you can break free of all your old patterns completely for a bit. But in general, try to select the healthiest ones and use slow and gentle protocols. I’d say one of the most abused psychedelics (aside from ketamine, if you call that a psychedelic) is 5-MeO-DMT. I have a guide on that. People very often believe you need a huge dose of it for a “full release.” They go through all kinds of screaming and shaking, nearly killing themselves, with absolutely zero inner-child work being done. It’s all spiritual bypassing.

path: Altered States Can Deepen the Therapy
If a past trip went badly
base_blocks.text: If a past trip went badly

path: Altered States Can Deepen the Therapy
If a past trip went badly
base_blocks.text: If you go manic, psychotic (by which I mean losing your sense of reality to the point of posing a risk to yourself or others), get super paranoid, or end up worse afterward than before, those are signs to reconsider trying the same thing again, and try to figure out why that happened. Don't try again until you understand what would make it safe. I’d look at the drug and the dosage, as well as mindset and setting etc.

path: Altered States Can Deepen the Therapy
Is your paranoia a warning sign?
base_blocks.text: Is your paranoia a warning sign?

path: Altered States Can Deepen the Therapy
Is your paranoia a warning sign?
base_blocks.text: Paranoia during a rough trip can be a warning sign for psychosis, but it doesn’t automatically lead there, since it can be valid. It tends to go that way when it isn’t balanced by practicality. “The CIA is mind-controlling me!” is paranoia. “The CIA, marketers, and other forces are conspiring to mind-control me, the way they do to everyone else! But since I can see that, I can prevent it to some extent, just by being aware of how it operates” is paranoia too, but it’s practically useful, and less likely to lead to psychosis. “...which means I can prevent it by standing on my head and counting backwards from 33, since 33 is their magic Freemason number!” is leaning psychotic. Some drugs are known for causing paranoia, like THC, so I’d avoid those.

path: Altered States Can Deepen the Therapy
Is your paranoia a warning sign?
base_blocks.text: If you can’t clearly understand what happened yourself, get someone qualified to help. And if you have an idea of what happened but aren’t sure, ask someone who knows you well.

path: Altered States Can Deepen the Therapy
If you might be prone to mania or psychosis
base_blocks.text: If you might be prone to mania or psychosis

path: Altered States Can Deepen the Therapy
If you might be prone to mania or psychosis
base_blocks.text: Any of those reactions, from mania to paranoia, can also point to a vulnerability in you, so I'd be careful with other drugs that mess with what's real too. And any predisposition toward mania or psychosis is a warning sign too, whether it's family history, a bad environment or a bad mindset. These are just caution signs, and when you see them, you take more precautions of every kind. You have to figure out what they mean for you, and if you can't, get help from trusted advisors.

path: Altered States Can Deepen the Therapy
base_blocks.text: Who counts as trusted

path: Altered States Can Deepen the Therapy
base_blocks.text: By trusted, I mean someone you know is trustworthy from a long relationship with them, not someone people on Reddit said was super magical and healing. That's called a crapshoot. It might turn out well, it might not. It might seem like it did, and then later you realize you were duped, as happened to me with Sidney the iboga shaman. A new therapist is not as trusted as an old one. As they say, "new friends are silver, but old friends are gold."

path: Altered States Can Deepen the Therapy
If you keep coming back from trips confused or spaced out
base_blocks.text: If you keep coming back from trips confused or spaced out

If you keep coming back from trips confused or spaced out
base_blocks.text: Maybe nothing worse happens, but after several trips like that I'd be concerned. If you're having episodes when you're sober, or any of them are severe, see a psychiatrist.

base_blocks.text: Before you quit a medication or alcohol

path: Altered States Can Deepen the Therapy
Before you quit a medication or alcohol
base_blocks.text: Don't suddenly stop a medication just because you suspect it's involved. Talk to the doctor who prescribed it. Benzos can be dangerous to quit cold turkey. Alcohol withdrawal can be dangerous if you're physically dependent.

path: Altered States Can Deepen the Therapy
base_blocks.text: What you mix

path: Altered States Can Deepen the Therapy
base_blocks.text: Be careful what you mix, too, and not just prescribed medicines. Even some basic things like cinnamon can be dangerous (and helpful) with ayahuasca, and doctors don't know about a lot of this. I also learned that mixing acacia confusa with mimosa hostilis is very destabilizing and challenging, but excellent if you want to know how it feels to be painfully autistic + schizo! I have a list of things to be cautious about with ayahuasca in particular.

path: Altered States Can Deepen the Therapy
base_blocks.text: Gentle Meditation and Mantra

path: Altered States Can Deepen the Therapy
base_blocks.text: Gentle meditation or self-hypnosis is a different story. It can really calm your nervous system down. A lot of people find that a mantra they feel some heart connection to, repeated in their head or out loud, especially with a nice melody, can lower the walls enough for the heart to open up. It's not something to lean on all day as a way of coping, but used as therapy it can be super effective. I personally love this beautiful Om Mane Pemme Hum mantra that I found in the Garchen Rinpoche documentary, For the Benefit of All Beings:

path: Altered States Can Deepen the Therapy
base_blocks.text: Altered States Can Require Reparenting

path: Altered States Can Deepen the Therapy
base_blocks.text: Have you ever been attacked by a literal demon? Maybe during sleep paralysis or meditation or on a psychedelic trip? A lot of modern folk laugh at this, yet it’s really quite a common experience. I was being psychically attacked by ghosts in my home as a child. Because I was literally a child, I was an easy target. And since most people never actually grew up, they are easy targets for every kind of influence, including spirit influence.

path: Altered States Can Deepen the Therapy
base_blocks.text: Those ghosts knew my weakness: dares. So they would dare me to jump out the window. I wasn’t suicidal, but I hated to seem like a “wussy.” Luckily, I trusted my parents with this information, and instead of taking me to a psychiatrist and pumping me full of anti-psychotic drugs, they put bars on the windows. Many kids are not so lucky in modern societies. They may get pumped full of anti-psychotic drugs for the rest of their life once diagnosed. That said, it'd make sense to get a professional to weigh in for some situations. I still played around with half-hanging out the windows, but I wasn’t quite dumb enough to jump out, and I really appreciate that my parents took it seriously without catastrophizing.

path: Altered States Can Deepen the Therapy
base_blocks.text: As a semi-adult, age 26, I discovered meditation. After I began meditating deeply for a while, it seemed like my astral portal opened. I started getting attacked by spirits during sleep paralysis. They would sit on me, prevent me from breathing, and instill tremendous fear into the core of my being.

path: Altered States Can Deepen the Therapy
base_blocks.text: Yep. Exactly like that.

path: Altered States Can Deepen the Therapy
base_blocks.text: Sleep paralysis is a trance-like state, and trance can be "more scary" because you're trapped in it, but it's also less actually dangerous. You can't ruin your life at all in trance (unless a bad hypnotic suggestion gets deeply implanted, perhaps), while without trance you can "freak out" in a way that might end up getting you committed to a mental hospital, thrown out of your housing, going to jail, possibly even killing yourself. In trance you can basically work with the fear. You recognize the fear has no real world significance and it's purely just fear, so it's super useful that way. The thing to fear is fear itself, since it actually opens us up to being manipulated by demons, which feed on it directly. So it's not really that they have no power. We give them the power.

path: Altered States Can Deepen the Therapy
base_blocks.text: After multiple episodes of this I decided to stop giving in to the victim mentality, and to start taking it seriously as a part of spiritual practice. My inner Guide saw it as a perfect opportunity to demonstrate the power of love over fear. The next time it happened, despite how scary it was, I sent unconditional love to this demon on me. It took some minutes, but once that love was seen as enduring, the demon left, and it never returned.

path: Altered States Can Deepen the Therapy
base_blocks.text: I’ve also trained other people to do this during spiritual attack while on psychedelics. It works a lot better if you are already trained in loving-kindness meditation to the point where it’s natural. I’d say it works way better than exorcism techniques (like Julian Palmer’s torping, which he also admits doesn’t work as well as love).

path: Altered States Can Deepen the Therapy
base_blocks.text: The astral plane is a bit different from the 3D. In the astral realm, unconditional love is a true, ultimately powerful physical force. Like a river, or a moat. There’s no evil that can trespass that moat. But don’t assume it will always work like that in the physical plane. It definitely has worked for me sometimes when facing some thugs, but definitely not with others. Loving someone does not mean you leave the front door unlocked with a sign saying “take whatever you want.”

path: Altered States Can Deepen the Therapy
base_blocks.text: If you’re not able yet (or in the moment) to summon real love for an enemy, you can first send love to your frightened little one from your adult Nurturer. Many people also find they can borrow support from God, Jesus, angels, devas, or whatever loving spiritual presence fits their tradition. If I were to do that, I would still be framing it as “Please help this situation with love” rather than “Strike down the enemy!” But if a presence seems to enjoy your fear, it's not one of your grown-ups, borrowed or not, whatever it says it is. Same goes if it demands you hurt or use anybody, yourself included.

path: Altered States Can Deepen the Therapy
base_blocks.text: Borrowing support like that is basically borrowed adulthood. At first you may need to feel protected or loved by something bigger than you, before that love starts to feel like yours, and then bit by bit it starts to become your own. Send some of it down to your frightened little one, and when that's possible, toward whatever you're afraid of. Continuing to relate to benevolent spiritual powers/beings is still perfectly fine, but they would surely be happy if they rubbed off on you!

path: Altered States Can Deepen the Therapy
base_blocks.text: If a voice or urge is directing you towards harm, and you feel at risk of acting on it, as with myself and those ghosts at home, move away from that open window and get some outside support.

base_blocks.text: Even social media algorithms will turn your life into hell if you don’t have the loving, protective inner parent developed. When you do, social media actually becomes useful and feels nice to interact with now and then.

path: Altered States Can Deepen the Therapy
Non-altered states can feel like this too
base_blocks.text: Many people think reparenting sounds silly, or like the kind of ridiculous therapy people do when they have too much time or money. But you know what’s even sillier? Wandering the world aimlessly and getting manipulated by all kinds of evil forces. 💀

base_blocks.text: My Psychedelic Experiences Came A Bit Too Soon

path: Altered States Can Deepen the Therapy
My Psychedelic Experiences Came A Bit Too Soon
base_blocks.text: The first time I took San Pedro cactus, at a medium-low dose, it made me super emotional, and I cried a lot. It was very therapeutic, actually. But I still squandered that opportunity: with a better understanding of reparenting, it could have been much more therapeutic.

path: Altered States Can Deepen the Therapy
My Psychedelic Experiences Came A Bit Too Soon
base_blocks.text: Ayahuasca was often much more challenging, because at first I was taking huge doses for ego death. The ayahuasca by itself wasn't exactly spiritual bypassing for me, though. It gave me a connection to divinity, and inner-child reparenting does work best with a little of that. But then I squandered the opportunity to bring that love down from the heavens to my inner child, which led me to be more like a preacher than a fully well-rounded individual who could lead by example.

path: Altered States Can Deepen the Therapy
My Psychedelic Experiences Came A Bit Too Soon
base_blocks.text: When you’re deeply entranced, you can’t freak out: no matter how scary something is, it’s just like, “Oh, this is scary, OK, oh well.” That’s not a good excuse to take crazy doses tho. I went psychotic once on ayahuasca made with pure THH (an alkaloid from the ayahuasca vine) and Mimosa hostilis bark, which has DMT in it. THH alone isn’t hypnotic (trance-like) enough to keep people safe with higher doses of DMT. I was very lucky that my landlord, a Quaker family friend, was super understanding and talked me down gently. Otherwise the cops might have been called, and I could still be in jail, perhaps, since ayahuasca was illegal there at the time, not to mention I had a bunch of mimosa bark in the house that they might have claimed was for distributing. In general, don’t call the cops and expect it to go well. That’s a real last resort.

path: Altered States Can Deepen the Therapy
My Psychedelic Experiences Came A Bit Too Soon
base_blocks.text: Out of hundreds of times I've taken iboga, there was one time just a small amount of male iboga root bark got me a bit hypomanic, to the point where a thought came: "Everyone should listen to me!" Luckily I was trained in Buddhist meditation, so I immediately challenged it with "Why should anyone listen if they have no interest?" I stopped using iboga for a while after that, and I warn people about that potential issue with male iboga specifically.

path: Altered States Can Deepen the Therapy
base_blocks.text: Physical Pain Makes It Harder

path: Altered States Can Deepen the Therapy
base_blocks.text: Physical pain can bring on the urge to escape too. Say an attack has you curled up on the bathroom floor, and whatever knocked the pain out last time (say, fent, or ketamine) starts looking real good, though you know it’ll leave you worse if you keep resorting to that quick fix.

path: Altered States Can Deepen the Therapy
base_blocks.text: By now, you may have already been through a million doctors who shrugged their shoulders, or even alternative treatments that were too costly or hard to grade. Sometimes it really is so simple that the best doctors and scanners can’t figure it out, like your house is moldy. It is worth going through all the basic checks first that you can do yourself, and trying the things that make most sense. For more on that, check my detox guide.

path: Altered States Can Deepen the Therapy
base_blocks.text: And when the symptoms come and go randomly, the best time to get diagnostics done could be right at the actual time of the crisis, rather than waiting until you feel well enough to make an appointment, and they may be able to treat it while it's happening. But what if the attacks come almost every day? You can’t move into the ER. And normal test results don’t prove the pain is imaginary, just as a treatment that helps doesn’t explain what’s causing it.

path: Altered States Can Deepen the Therapy
base_blocks.text: I’d ask for a chronic pain specialist and a written plan for the flare-ups you can see coming, including the new or severe signs that mean you go to the ER right away, but don’t let amelioration of symptoms be the end of the investigation.

path: Altered States Can Deepen the Therapy

base_blocks.text: Listen To Your Body, Or Else!

path: Altered States Can Deepen the Therapy
Listen To Your Body, Or Else!
base_blocks.text: Sometimes, a physical illness is really partly or wholly an emotional issue causing “somatic symptoms,” as happened to various friends of mine, as well as to Lucia Capacchione, PhD., and many of her clients and friends. She wrote one of the first comprehensive inner child therapy guides, Recovery of Your Inner Child, in 1991. While I don’t doubt that many people do recover from mysterious physical illness via meditation, inner child therapy, and somatic therapy, I also don’t want to claim, as some folks do, that all illness is entirely rooted in emotional issues. That is clearly not true. We don’t need to be gaslit to consider all the possibilities.

path: If You Want to Kill Yourself
base_blocks.text: If You Want to Kill Yourself

path: If You Want to Kill Yourself
base_blocks.text: Maybe you're reading this about to act, or with the means close by. Then before anything else, get another human being involved, and put some distance between you and the means. A crisis line counts, and the person on the other end can be a total stranger. Do the same if you can't stop yourself, or you're badly disoriented or intoxicated. Can't tell if that's you? Treat it like it is. None of that is me answering whether life is worth living. It just keeps the question open long enough to look at.

path: If You Want to Kill Yourself
base_blocks.text: Then, before getting all philosophical, make sure there's a real, live grown-up in the room or on the phone, if that's possible. And as for the internal psychology of it, when the part that wants to die feels like all of you, go ahead and notice who's doing the noticing (as we discussed in Noticing Counts), or borrow an adult from the adult lending library in your head :). Any part of you that can help keep your body safe, or would rather wait on a decision you can't undo, is welcome. And if none of them shows up yet? No problem, the questions can wait.

path: If You Want to Kill Yourself
The Spiritual Side of the Question
base_blocks.text: The Spiritual Side of the Question

path: If You Want to Kill Yourself
The Spiritual Side of the Question
base_blocks.text: I try not to proselytize about spirituality, because I've made that mistake before, and I now see that it's better to let folks find it when they are ready. But when someone tells me they want to kill themself, I consider the topic to be brutally opened by default, regardless of whether they meant to do that, because if they actually do kill their body (which they might mistake to be their self), that's a very powerful spiritual challenge right there, even if they didn't realize it would be.

path: If You Want to Kill Yourself
The Spiritual Side of the Question
base_blocks.text: Then ask: what is the self you want to kill? Is that self the same thing as your body? Why? Do you have the same body in dreams? What exactly do you expect your body’s death to accomplish? If the problem is a state of mind, like self-hatred or despair, shame or loneliness, what makes you so sure that destroying the body ends it?

path: If You Want to Kill Yourself
The Spiritual Side of the Question
base_blocks.text: In Buddhism, death isn’t an off switch, and it isn’t a free new-age get-out-of-jail card back to the source. Repeated thought and intention shape the mind, and that keeps going through death and rebirth. Yes, that can include hell realms. A human birth is a rare chance to understand suffering and end its causes.

path: If You Want to Kill Yourself
The Spiritual Side of the Question
base_blocks.text: You don’t have to believe that, but if you’re still thinking of staking your life on the opposite claim, that death is just nothing, might that be a double standard to look into? Curiosity killed the cat, you might say, so research could be dangerous. 😅 But despite the risk of curiosity, researchers at the University of Virginia have been busy little bees, collecting cases for 60 YEARS now of young kids who talk about a past life, and there’s a big pile of near-death accounts too. Even if every case is different, but I’d read a few of those cases before betting my life on “nothing.”

path: If You Want to Kill Yourself
The Spiritual Side of the Question
base_blocks.text: Right here in this one life, it's apparent that the more you hate yourself, the better your mind gets at it, and being alone tends to deepen the despair. But lucky us, because physical life keeps handing out redirections, like that guy who found me in a random park crying one time, and asked me "What's wrong?" If the many traditions and the accumulating scientific evidence are right that the mind’s causal process goes on after the body dies, killing the body may take away some of those redirections and leave the suffering right where it was. That sounds like a substantially worse deal to me.

path: If You Want to Kill Yourself
The Spiritual Side of the Question
base_blocks.text: My father used to tell suicidal people, “Oh, you want to kill yourself? That’s wonderful! Now you can change what you’ve always been too afraid to change in your life, and then see if you still want to end it!” So, what would you tell my dad? What’s the change you still can’t bring yourself to make? Leaving a relationship? Quitting a job? Telling your family who you really are? Those might sound difficult, but they're actually considerably more likely to help than dying.

base_blocks.text: As I mentioned in my nibbana article, I’ve had my most profound spiritual peak experiences and realizations when I had the least interest in continued existence. And the Buddha taught in MN 129, attaining a human birth is as rare and precious as it would be for a one-eyed turtle to pop his head up through a hoop on the surface of the vast ocean. You won the cosmic jackpot, so don’t throw away the ticket before you open the envelope to find it!

base_blocks.text: Sometimes There Isn't a Clear Child Yet

path: Sometimes There Isn't a Clear Child Yet
base_blocks.text: Reparenting assumes there's a clear little one in there to love, and for a lot of people there is. But if you grew up somewhere you only belonged as long as you played somebody else, like a really controlling family or a strict church, the real one may never have had room to form. All this stuff about your little one could have left you wondering who I'm even talking about.

path: Sometimes There Isn't a Clear Child Yet
base_blocks.text: Maybe you started playing that part so early, and it took over so completely, that "What do I believe?" or "What do I want?" has no clear answer of your own. They sound like such easy questions, too. Back then, asking might have gotten you in trouble, or laughed at. Or there was just no way to ask. That can make "love yourself" feel pretty empty (love what, when the part you've been playing doesn't feel real?).

path: Sometimes There Isn't a Clear Child Yet
base_blocks.text: From Survival to Experimental Play

path: Sometimes There Isn't a Clear Child Yet
base_blocks.text: If your childhood meant avoiding pain and keeping the people you needed close, your attention got used up reading danger (was that sigh about me?) and meeting their expectations, and when curiosity or mistakes got you punished, or it felt like they loved you less, you got better at the part. That left much less room for experiments that show you what you like when nobody's grading you. People grow into who they are by trying things on and then changing their minds, from what they wear down to the ideas and roles they take up, like a teenager who starts spelling her name with an "i" at the end and later changes it back.

path: Sometimes There Isn't a Clear Child Yet
base_blocks.text: Some of this is developmental pl/ork you get to do late: making it safe enough for your curiosity and experimenting to finally grow, and your preferences too. It might feel wrong somehow to like something before you've checked anyone's face. You can usually reparent and build who you are at the same time.

path: Sometimes There Isn't a Clear Child Yet
base_blocks.text: As you tell the part you've been playing apart from the self that didn't get much practice, notice whether it makes you more curious about both, and better able to relate to them. Or does it have you thinking, "That one's fake, and I'm getting rid of it"? You're after a relationship between them inside you that works better, and that's hard to have if there's a new split between an acceptable self and one that has to disappear.

path: Sometimes There Isn't a Clear Child Yet
base_blocks.text: When you ask what your little one feels, maybe all you get is a guess, which isn't proof there's no little one in there. Maybe you hear yourself answer, "Scared? I mean, it would make sense if it was scared."

path: Sometimes There Isn't a Clear Child Yet
base_blocks.text: So early on, the practice is finding out who's actually in there, through long reflection with no outside input, and journaling just for yourself, without picturing a reader. You might catch yourself explaining who everybody is anyway. Time alone in nature helps too, and so does getting back the preferences that got buried: the foods you really like and what feels good to do, and what you believe and feel when nobody's around to take your cues from. Focusing (Eugene Gendlin's method of listening to a vague, felt sense in your body) can especially help you notice feelings and preferences the part you've been playing learned to overlook. Any words you put to them can stay tentative ("I hate cooking... or just for everybody?") while you look at what they seem to mean and revise how you read them.

path: Sometimes There Isn't a Clear Child Yet
base_blocks.text: Untangling the Belonging Bargains

path: Sometimes There Isn't a Clear Child Yet
base_blocks.text: Part of building who you are is untangling yourself from whatever pulls you away from your own knowing in return for belonging. A political tribe might expect consistent positions and predictable reactions, while a family or religion that's kind to you might have expectations that just feel like being good. Most groups expect some conformity. Your family might want a particular kind of son or daughter, and your friends might have rules about what you can joke about or get upset about. But if going along means betraying yourself, that's the bargain. It can help to write down the rules your family ran on, including unspoken ones like "Boys don't cry." Then write down the role you got handed, like the stand-in parent, or the one who got blamed for everything (ST-CA has lists of both, in sections 15.2.3 and 15.2.4).

path: Sometimes There Isn't a Clear Child Yet
base_blocks.text: Then there's another bargain, where you have to earn your worth: when you don't feel your value inside as a human being, you can become a "human doer," working for it in some arena outside yourself. That might be beauty, athleticism, sexual desirability, intelligence or grades. For some people it's money or status, and for others it's a sophisticated spiritual identity or becoming indispensable to everybody else's problems. It can feel really good to be the one everybody calls. In the more shadowy presentation, when you really need to feel needed, you might be like the firefighters who become arsonists to keep themselves employed.

path: Sometimes There Isn't a Clear Child Yet
base_blocks.text: Even with good parents, you could have learned unhealthy self-valuation when people repeatedly praised what you did rather than your inherent worth. That wasn't your flaw. In the process of self-differentiation, we learn to notice when we're making the trade, and we begin keeping our ground more when feasible.

path: Sometimes There Isn't a Clear Child Yet
When Being Happy Feels Like Abandoning Someone
base_blocks.text: When Being Happy Feels Like Abandoning Someone

path: Sometimes There Isn't a Clear Child Yet
When Being Happy Feels Like Abandoning Someone
base_blocks.text: Some families run on a bargain like "If I'm happy while someone I love is suffering, I'm abandoning them."

path: Sometimes There Isn't a Clear Child Yet
When Being Happy Feels Like Abandoning Someone
base_blocks.text: That's exactly why I was crying for 14 years. Beginning at the age of 12, when I really started to understand that life is brutal for most people, I became convinced that being happy myself, while others weren't, was selfish. I had this poster in my room that really resonated with me, by the famous socialist, Eugene V. Debs. I told this to a therapist in college and she actually agreed it was a good reason to be depressed!

path: Sometimes There Isn't a Clear Child Yet
When Being Happy Feels Like Abandoning Someone
base_blocks.text: What I found, once I started cultivating my own happiness, was that I got a lot better at helping other people toward theirs. Do your part for people who are suffering, and skip the part where you have to be miserable too.

path: Sometimes There Isn't a Clear Child Yet
When Being Happy Feels Like Abandoning Someone
base_blocks.text: Some friends or family really might not like it when you get happier, though. Someone might pull away, or keep dragging you back into the old misery. I'd take that loss seriously, and look at what they do and what you owe them, before deciding it's envy.

path: Sometimes There Isn't a Clear Child Yet
When Being Happy Feels Like Abandoning Someone
base_blocks.text: I'd still try a small good thing, like a nice meal, and see what actually happens.

path: Sometimes There Isn't a Clear Child Yet
Four Pairs That Commonly Hook the Child
base_blocks.text: Four Pairs That Commonly Hook the Child

path: Sometimes There Isn't a Clear Child Yet
Four Pairs That Commonly Hook the Child
base_blocks.text: Pema Chödrön has a quick map for finding the bargain. It's four pairs, starting with pleasure and pain, and gain and loss. The other two are about what people think of you: praise and blame, and good reputation and disgrace. Your little one can panic when something hurts, and also when something good might disappear, like praise, romance, money, status, belonging or a spiritual high. You might still be enjoying one of those when your little one starts asking how long this is going to last.

path: Sometimes There Isn't a Clear Child Yet
Four Pairs That Commonly Hook the Child
base_blocks.text: When that happens, you can ask yourself these, once you've caught your breath:

path: Sometimes There Isn't a Clear Child Yet
Four Pairs That Commonly Hook the Child
base_blocks.text:
- What do I think I'm about to get, or lose?
- Whose approval suddenly feels like I can't live without it? It isn't always who you'd guess.
- Is this a value I'm standing up for, or a high I'm trying to keep?
- Would this still be something I'd feel is worth doing if at the end of the day, I didn't get praise from anyone for it?

path: Sometimes There Isn't a Clear Child Yet
Four Pairs That Commonly Hook the Child
base_blocks.text: You don't have to stop enjoying pleasure, praise, gain or belonging. The question is whether losing one of them would feel like losing yourself.

path: Sometimes There Isn't a Clear Child Yet
Four Pairs That Commonly Hook the Child
base_blocks.text: Differentiation

path: Sometimes There Isn't a Clear Child Yet
Four Pairs That Commonly Hook the Child
base_blocks.text: Differentiation can happen right inside a family, religion, community or relationship. You'd still belong, just selectively. As a differentiated adult you can stay deeply embedded, free to question things or disagree. If a parent used to go quiet and hurt whenever you disagreed, that might be hard to believe. A family where everyone gets to be their own person is healthier than an enmeshed one, and a faith that's your own is healthier than religious compliance. It can be the same religion either way. And two differentiated people have a sturdier relationship than two who've been absorbed into each other.

path: Sometimes There Isn't a Clear Child Yet
Four Pairs That Commonly Hook the Child
base_blocks.text: Day to day, differentiation looks something like this:

path: Sometimes There Isn't a Clear Child Yet
Four Pairs That Commonly Hook the Child
base_blocks.text:
- Caring about somebody's feelings without automatically adopting their opinions or sacrificing your own ground. Their reasons can still change your mind, though.
- Noticing when you agreed in the moment and disagree later: "Wait, why was I nodding along?"
- Noticing when what you thought you knew suddenly feels like water dripping through your hand because of praise or pity, fear or attraction, or something that really resonates with you.
- Disappointing people and withstanding social pressure, and still being recognizably yourself wherever you are (maybe louder in some places). That one can take a while.
- Questioning what you were programmed to believe while holding the discomfort, and without having to stop loving anyone over it.

path: Sometimes There Isn't a Clear Child Yet
Four Pairs That Commonly Hook the Child
base_blocks.text: Differentiation is slow, and it goes on your whole life. Sometimes you need to take a break from a family, group or relationship, even if they aren't doing anything to you. Simply being around them may pull you into that programmed space where listening to what you really want becomes harder. Some people come back later on different terms, and sometimes the break has to be long-term because the pattern of losing yourself with them is deeply entrenched. As you differentiate, you learn to tell which of those apply.

path: Sometimes There Isn't a Clear Child Yet
Four Pairs That Commonly Hook the Child
base_blocks.text: Key developed this identity and differentiation portion of the method, drawing on Murray Bowen's family-systems work and her own self-therapy.

path: Sometimes There Isn't a Clear Child Yet
Let the Child Be Bad at Things
base_blocks.text: Let the Child Be Bad at Things

path: Sometimes There Isn't a Clear Child Yet
Let the Child Be Bad at Things
base_blocks.text: Reflection can show you what got sMothered (typo?) or suppressed. For identity you also need some experiments out in real life, so go try something new just for you. Maybe a foraging group, or a painting class. Stargazing can be awe-inspiring, and you might even see a UFO! Notice what holds your attention when nobody is impressed.

path: Sometimes There Isn't a Clear Child Yet
Let the Child Be Bad at Things
base_blocks.text: The old parent in your head may demand immediate talent, though, and then the first time you're awkward at it, that's "evidence" that you're stupid or clumsy. Or you hear, "Come on, you're not really the type." I think your little one is listening to see if anybody's going to stick up for them. The grown-up you're building has to be the one who does: "It's okay if we're bad at this, nobody's on trial. We're just seeing if we like it."

path: Sometimes There Isn't a Clear Child Yet
Let the Child Be Bad at Things
base_blocks.text: Give a new interest enough tries to get past the humiliation of being a beginner, when you keep telling people, "Sorry, I'm new." Maybe after that you still genuinely dislike it, and then you may quit. You may also discover a part of yourself that never had permission to exist.
The Inner Guide

As the Guide, you choose what your little one learns and what it gets to experience, and you hold standards, the way a good parent would. Your parent's harsh tone doesn't come with the job, though. You ask hard things of it so it can grow, at its own pace. That's what I was just asking of you, with that new interest. You also widen its world with art and music, and you point out beautiful things when you see them. Nature is part of that, and so is the wider world past the end of the street you grew up on.
By the way, this job doesn't have to be called the Guide. The Wise One works, or your Inner Teacher, and "Guru" does for some people.
Between Spoiling and Clamping Down

Maybe you've let a small child win at Go Fish and never found a good time to start playing for real. Who wants to be the grown-up who finally wins? Without the Guide, you can slide from looking after your little one into spoiling it the same way. Sweets and screens can pass for loving yourself, and so can getting it out of anything hard. Treats and pampering do better at set times, where they can't get out of hand. They shouldn't get canceled as a punishment after a bad day, either (ST-CA, section 17.1.4).

After all, sometimes “I want it NOW!” is just that: a rung on the desire treadmill. No hidden guard or old trauma required, because all creatures have endless desires naturally anyway, especially when immature. You can hear that want without shame about it. Hearing it doesn’t require giving into it, especially if getting your way would hurt you or somebody else.

I think the opposite trap can feel a lot like finally having your act together. It's forced adulthood, and it sounds like "Nope, all good!" from somebody with a fever who's cleaning the whole kitchen anyway. Not a lot of fun in that kitchen, and nobody gets very close to the person in it. If that's you, clamping down harder is going to feel like the fix, but it's just more of the same. I'd try croaking to someone you trust, "Could you pick up some soup?" If you keep swinging between spoiling and clamping down, try staying warm while you say what happens next, like "Not now, we'll go after lunch."

Once a need does show, after all that hiding, it's okay to want a lot of closeness. So then someone you love goes for a walk alone, and you've texted "hello??" before they're at the corner. When they get back, you sulk all night. Wanting them close is fine! But they get to go for a walk too. Ask your little one what it's afraid of. I think it just wants to know they're coming back. Then the Guide can come up with something like "See you in an hour?"

path: A Healthy Mind Is Not a Perfect Mind
base_blocks.text: A Healthy Mind Is Not a Perfect Mind

path: A Healthy Mind Is Not a Perfect Mind
base_blocks.text: The Guide doesn't need to know everything for sure (that would be an OCD Guide, and then you'd need a Guide for the OCD Guide). It chooses the next sane step that fits your values based on the info available, and that's how it helps your little one grow toward a whole life. Waiting to be sure first is sometimes proper & prudent, but if it's a pattern, it can keep life on hold, and then your little one's world stays small. Sometimes something really is stuck on someone else's end (you've asked, and followed up, and there's nothing left for you to do yet), and waiting on that isn't avoidance. The Guide can let it wait, keeping an eye out for when it frees up, and keep the rest of your life moving, so your little one keeps growing anyway.

path: A Healthy Mind Is Not a Perfect Mind
base_blocks.text: Forced adulthood can get into your head too, where it wants everything as spotless as that kitchen. At your grandpa's funeral, some dumb jingle starts up in your head and you nearly laugh during the eulogy. That doesn't mean you didn't love him, or that something's wrong with you. Minds come up with ugly and embarrassing stuff all the time, some of it the opposite of what you believe, and bodies do their own thing too. The Guide isn't there to police every thought. It notices the jingle and knows you didn't mean it, and that it isn't who you are. Then it goes with what you'd stand behind, which here is probably squeezing your mom's hand and listening, and lets the jingle go.

path: A Healthy Mind Is Not a Perfect Mind
base_blocks.text: I think this is closer to Buddhist practice too. The point is not an impossible performance in which nothing unskillful ever appears. In one discourse (sutta), AN 6.63, the Buddha defines karma in terms of intention (so if you didn't mean to cause harm, your mind is not poisoned). In DN 2, he explains that in the training to purify the mind, one first recognizes a fault, makes amends, and then restrains themself to prevent that kind of thing in future. So it's not like, "you're either pure, or you're not," which is where a lot of folks stay stuck. If you're ashamed about something you chose to do, that might be a signal to give some attention to that. If it's shame just because of an intrusive thought, then it's probably not adaptive and can be simply let go of.
You Belong Everywhere and Nowhere

The Guide also points beyond itself, toward somewhere you belong that doesn’t ask you to give up being yourself. That might be nature, or existence itself. It might be whatever your tradition sees as ultimate. Love can come from any of these places, and you also belong there, which is a little different. Maybe you’ve felt that outside somewhere, like you didn’t need anybody’s okay to be there. The way in is time in nature and contemplative practice, like meditation.

With that under you, belonging with people can get a lot less desperate. Your little one might still think, “If they stop liking me, I won’t belong anywhere,” and the Guide can remind it there’s more to belong to than them.
Timing Is Individual

Most of us need enough Nurturer and Protector first. Otherwise the Guide just overrules your little one in the name of something higher (spiritual bypassing, dressed up as direction). Like a shepherd who's beating sheep to make them move. So warmth and safety come first for a while, and the direction can grow once there's a clear little one in there to guide.

Say you had a spiritual opening years before you had much of a Nurturer or Protector (openings can come that early, and yours may have been completely real). Has your love grown because of it, and has that love reached your little one yet? Look at how you are with people, too, whether you’re more compassionate and do more to protect them. Are you getting better at relationships, including telling the truth when it’s awkward and doing what you said you’d do?

path: How Much Happiness Do You Know Is Possible?
base_blocks.text: How Much Happiness Do You Know Is Possible?

path: How Much Happiness Do You Know Is Possible?
base_blocks.text: When you wish someone well, what do you have in mind? Probably something like, “I want them to have enough to eat, a safe place to sleep, some people who like them, etc.” Wanting this for someone is a form of love (this is the kind babies already understand). It’s a good and important thing, this practical love. But the horizon of your wishes may be partly determined by how much happiness/peace/freedom you know to be possible.

path: How Much Happiness Do You Know Is Possible?
base_blocks.text: Sometimes your little one already feels cared for in the normal ways, well fed, good boundaries at work, but will either of these actually deal with the existential issue? Maybe your life isn’t meant to be just something to put up with, something to slog through, a hamster wheel, a rat race. Maybe you could live it with a sense of zest and discovery. What would you need for that?

path: How Much Happiness Do You Know Is Possible?
base_blocks.text: Maybe you’ve had some big spiritual experiences, and for a while knew a kind of peace/love etc. that you hadn’t known before. Now when you wish someone well, your wishes may be bigger – perhaps much bigger – than they would have been before. This is one reason why loving-kindness meditation can seem kind of silly (who doesn’t want people to be happy!?) but actually be very powerful. Saying, “May you be happy,” over and over won’t necessarily zap you into a state of profound love for all beings, but it’s one way people discover that there is such a love and learn to expand it.

path: How Much Happiness Do You Know Is Possible?
base_blocks.text: If you’re curious about this bigger happiness, follow that curiosity. You don’t have to pretend to believe anything, but you might read a few people from different traditions (try a Sufi poet or a Zen teacher). If you know anyone who seems consistently happy in this bigger way, check out how they deal with people when things are going badly. And if they still pass that test, consider, "I don’t know if I believe their explanation. But what if the experience is possible for me?”

path: How Much Happiness Do You Know Is Possible?
base_blocks.text: Somatic Heart Opening

path: How Much Happiness Do You Know Is Possible?
base_blocks.text: Rumi says you have to keep breaking your heart until it stays open. Some people find that deep grieving gives way to warmth, or to feeling connected. Some feel held, in the body. Being loved can open grief, too. Someone takes care of you, and you think, "Why does this make me sad?" It can be sadness for the care that was missing. While you're present and still choosing, stay with it. Once it's swamping you instead of opening you, slow down (like turning the song off for the night).

path: How Much Happiness Do You Know Is Possible?
When the Practice Feels Real but Stays Shallow
base_blocks.text: When the Practice Feels Real but Stays Shallow

path: How Much Happiness Do You Know Is Possible?
When the Practice Feels Real but Stays Shallow
base_blocks.text: Some people have the opposite problem, where it feels like they’re connecting with their little boo, but then they find out somehow that it was still pretty superficial. Dreams can open up much more emotionally direct stuff, especially in the second half of the night's sleep, if you wake up in the middle to meditate, as I've discovered. That's a good point to ponder over what the dream let you feel that the session didn’t, and look at it again in the morning (but write it down so you remember!). And if nightmares start wrecking your sleep, shorten the practice or do it earlier.
Borrowed Adulthood in Relationship

Reparenting is usually talked about as something you do alone, or with a therapist. But your little one got hurt by people, so some of the healing has to happen with people too. Often it's mostly one person carrying a lot of it, maybe the one who drives you to your appointments and says it'll be okay. Maybe you're picturing them right now. Having someone like that while you're struggling can be an enormous blessing. If it's more distributed, with various people you can count on for small parts, that can be more sustainable, even if it doesn't feel as monumental.

Over time, reparenting can help you take in some of what they've been doing for you, and start doing it yourself, even that calendar bit. What you're after is care your little one can count on from more than one place, while the inner relationship stays precious and important. Other jobs can go to friends or community, outsource to the tools or pros, whatever works. You'll find the balance is dynamic between inner & outer reliance, and going too far in either extreme isn't generally the healthiest.
Dating While You Heal

Maybe you’d rather that your support person were a lover, as well. Lots of people open a dating app in the middle of the night, hoping someone will make it all stop hurting. 🙈 If that’s you right now, dating can wait while your friends and the steady people around you do their part. That doesn’t mean you have to be completely healed before you date, but romance should follow when two people really love each other and want to build a life together. It won’t rescue you from the pain or reward you for healing, and it sucks to mess up a beautiful relationship because of unhealed trauma, believe me, I know. I wrote a whole romance guide, mostly due to this.
First Social Connections, Done Right

Then there are people you’re just getting to know. Meeting them can turn into a kind of test--”First impressions are everything,” as they say, but it could be even worse than that, if you need them to prove you’re lovable. Nobody’s a reassurance machine. I’m giving you permission now to quit school and flunk the tests. Instead, get curious about who this person is, and who you are, and let both of you have your own reasons for being there in the beautiful present. Leaning on each other is still a big part of relationships, and it goes both ways.

I can’t tell you where to look for people who fit you, but I’d bet on more than one place. Keep the good people you’ve already got. Then maybe try a class, or a spiritual community if you find one that fits you. And if any group, or any one person, starts acting like they should be your only support, that’s when we ask the Adult Protector to start paying attention.

The same goes for doctors. No need to give them a good impression if that means not being your own advocate. If you don't feel up to it, bring someone you trust to speak up for you (it doesn’t have to be the relative who never respected your wishes), and ask what a treatment’s for.

path: Opening up honestly to the right people at the right pace
base_blocks.text: Opening up honestly to the right people at the right pace

path: Opening up honestly to the right people at the right pace
base_blocks.text: And reaching out doesn't mean telling strangers everything. Privacy isn't fakery. People can earn more of you by how they handle the smaller stuff, like whether that thing you told them about your weird fear of birds turns into a joke at the next party 🙈, and how they take it when you say no. But if a relationship is getting deep and you're still keeping up a fake normal, happy version of yourself to hold onto it, I'd either bring more of the truth in, carefully, or let it be less deep for now. (If telling could put you in real danger, like violence, or being outed where that isn't safe, protect yourself first.) And when someone finally accepts you, it can feel amazing. It still doesn't prove you're meant for each other, or that they've earned your trust yet.

base_blocks.text: Before You Tell the Hardest Stuff

path: Opening up honestly to the right people at the right pace
Before You Tell the Hardest Stuff
base_blocks.text: Then there’s the stuff that’s hardest to tell anyone, and of course that's exactly what you need help with. Maybe it’s an urge that scares you, or something you did that could get you in legal trouble. I'd assume that what you tell won't be completely confidential, especially if it sounds like something dangerous.

path: Opening up honestly to the right people at the right pace
Before You Tell the Hardest Stuff
base_blocks.text: You know that DM you deleted? It can still be sitting on their phone as a screenshot 🙈, and whatever’s on a company’s server can get handed over if a court asks. Just because Mr. Boopaloopa was your name on WhatsApp doesn't guarantee you're anonymous, by the way.

path: Opening up honestly to the right people at the right pace
Before You Tell the Hardest Stuff
base_blocks.text: And some of the people you’d tell, like therapists, teachers, and doctors, can be required to report certain things (a few laws cover everybody, too). Which things depends on where you live, and it’s nowhere near every crime you might mention. The cops are hopefully the obvious ones to be careful with, even if they pretend to care.

path: Opening up honestly to the right people at the right pace
Before You Tell the Hardest Stuff
base_blocks.text: So I’d ask this person, before handing over any tricky specifics: “What does the law require you to report?” That's a normal and expected question. Although personally I wouldn't even bother with that, because whatever they tell you today, the law can change tomorrow.

path: Opening up honestly to the right people at the right pace
Before You Tell the Hardest Stuff
base_blocks.text: You can always rephrase things as a dream narrative to get the emotional content across without triggering alarm bells (although I actually got in trouble with TalkSpace therapy bot even for a dream!). Just don’t hold back a danger that’s happening now from people who can help, and get anyone in danger safe before worrying about the rest. Sometimes telling on yourself is the thing that keeps someone safe, whatever it costs you legally.
Other Folks Also Have Hooks

Once you're in your happy place, look at the other person too, and don't go only by the one fight where they crossed your boundary, or, the other way around, by the one "no" or boundary of theirs that made you mad — after all, they're allowed to say no to you. Does it keep ending the same way, where you bring up something that hurt and then still end up reassuring them they're not a bad person, and the talk never comes back to what happened to you? (The psychologist Lindsay Gibson wrote the book on this: Disentangling from Emotionally Immature People.) Or can they hear you disagree and look at their own part?

If it's the first, it can seem like you haven't explained yourself well enough yet. You probably have, and it makes more sense to count on what they keep showing you they can do than on the right words finally getting through to them. Maybe what they can do is text you something kind the next day and not bring any of it up.
Can they change?

You may not know for certain whether the other person is or could be capable of a healthier response, and neither do they. If they promise to change, that's probably as useful as their prior promises were. Think about how long it has taken you to become more healthy. Could you have done that from one moment to the next based on a promise? Sometimes we can be a better support for someone when we maintain a realistic boundary, so that we can hold high expectations, and still feel prepared for their failure to meet them.

path: If you really did hurt them
base_blocks.text: You can mean the apology for a start. Then notice what happens next. Are you sorry for what you did, or are you starting to take back the complaint too because they're still upset? Maybe your first explanation sucked. Try again. 😅 And if it fails again, and you've said what you mean, well, you can't guarantee they'll understand it. Guilt may keep shouting at you. That doesn't tell you the whole conflict was your fault, nor does it prove they're manipulating you.
